items.title: Finite regulated Newtonian gravitational canonical preparation
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement: Work in SI units. Adopt positive Newton constant $G$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, common particle mass $m$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, positions $q_i$ in $\mathrm m$, momenta $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy $H$ in joules, Boltzmann constant $k_B$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. Fix an action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$; it is a phase-counting convention, not an assertion that $h_*$ equals Planck's constant. These conventions follow [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]].
items.physical_scope: Finite N≥2, bounded positive-volume confining box, equal classical masses, fixed positive softening length and inverse-energy parameter; effective Newtonian weak-field/slow-motion model only, with no thermalization or dynamical stability claim.

items.title: Constructed finite canonical gravitational equilibrium
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement: Fix $N\ge2$, a bounded measurable box $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $0<|B|<\infty$, $m,G,a,k_B,h_*>0$, $a>0$, and $\beta>0$. Adopt the physical preparation in [[post-tgr-finite-newton-gravity-preparation]] with its fixed Hamiltonian $H_{N,a}$ and reference measure $\nu_N$. Conditional on the exact current mathematical interfaces in [[lem-tgr-finite-gravitational-gibbs]], [[thm-tgr-finite-gravitational-entropy-optimum]], and [[thm-tgr-gravitational-canonical-response]], the partition function $Z_N(\beta)=\int e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}d\nu_N$ is finite and positive, and $p_\beta=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}$ is a normalized density.
items.physical_scope: Conditional on the finite equal-mass softened Newtonian model with bounded positive-volume box and fixed a>0; proves normalization, the stated Gibbs variational optimum, and nonnegative fixed-Hamiltonian canonical response, not thermalization or stability of a changing/self-consistent background.

items.statement: Use the same positive relative parameters $\mu,A,r_0,R,h_*$ and fixed Hamiltonian $h(q,p)=|p|^2/(2\mu)-A/|q|$ for both preparations in [[post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-preparation]] and [[post-tgr-kepler-canonical-preparation]]. Let $R>32r_0$, choose $E=-e=-A/(32r_0)$, and assume the microcanonical physical applicability condition
items.physical_scope: Same fixed relative Kepler Hamiltonian and radial shell, with Gibbs-volume microcanonical versus canonical preparation. At E=−A/(32r0), R>32r0, and 2A/(μr0c²)≤δNR≪1, the microcanonical branch is slow-motion and has CG<0; the canonical model has CK≥0 but retains unbounded momentum tails. No equivalence or thermalization is asserted.

items.title: Prepared finite softened two-body ensemble

items.statement: Take $B=(0,L)^3$ with $L>0$, $N=2$, equal mass $m>0$, Newton constant $G>0$, softening length $a>0$, action reference $h_*>0$, and $\beta>0$. Use the finite softened Newtonian preparation and its fixed Hamiltonian and measure.
items.physical_scope: One explicit finite box and positive softening instance of the adopted effective Newtonian preparation; establishes a normalized model probability, not observed equilibration or a claim about a real gravitating gas.

items.physical_scope: Refutes finite-volume sufficiency for the exact unregulated two-point Newtonian canonical weight, for arbitrary positive masses. The collision limit is outside a controlled weak-field Newtonian regime and is not asserted to describe a real short-distance source.

items.title: Confined negative-capacity Kepler preparation
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement: Choose $m_1,m_2>0$, $A=Gm_1m_2$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, inner radius $r_0>0$, and outer radius $R>32r_0$. Set $E=-A/(32r_0)$ and assume $2A/(\mu r_0c^2)\le\delta_{\rm NR}\ll1$. Use the two preparations and response conventions of the A-page comparison theorem.
items.physical_scope: One energy and shell-radius instance of the finite regulated relative Kepler model under its declared Gibbs-volume convention and weak-field restriction; the canonical comparison remains a distinct preparation with unbounded momenta.

items.title: Fixed lapse two gas normalization
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement: Let $B=(0,L)^3$ with $L>0$, $I_{x^0}\subset\mathbb R$ open, $h_{ij}=\delta_{ij}$, and constant dimensionless lapse $\mathcal N=2$ on the prescribed static metric $g=-4(dx^0)^2+\delta_{ij}dx^idx^j$, with $x^0=ct$. Since the metric coefficients are independent of $x^0$, choose the Killing generator $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ to define $T_K=(k_B\beta_K)^{-1}$, where $\beta_K>0$. This fixes a normalization convention for the generator; $T_K$ is not identified with the proper temperature at the wall.
items.physical_scope: Classical ideal gas on a prescribed flat finite box with constant dimensionless lapse two and a stated Killing-generator normalization; the local temperature parameter is T_K/2 and is not a reported measurement.
